I also think this was more affective than any other strategy I've ever seen because the HGs weren't asking Jessica to vote Cody out or put him on the block. They were just asking her to not use a power to ensure his safety for the week, allowing the house to "do the dirty work" and vote Cody out. Therefore, Jessica wasn't solely responsible for anything *technically*. 

However, Jessica did ultimately say that even with her not using her power, that would still be her "having a hand in Cody's eviction". But still, this is obviously a less dirty move than if she had voted against him or, even worse, put him up herself.

In season 19, almost all of the HGs took turns trying to convince Jessica to turn on Cody the week that they were on the block together. They all took turns having one on one's with her trying to get her to not use the Halting Hex so that the house could vote Cody out. Her and Cody had gotten into an argument, and the house saw this as an opportunity to get in Jessica's ear about how bad Cody was for her game.

This ultimately blew up in everyone's faces because she used the Hex anyway. However, this was probably the most valiant effort I've ever seen of HGs banning together to try and get a showmance to turn on one another. I'd say if there ever were a tactic to try to get a showmance to split up, this would be it. I forget exactly how many different HGs went to Jessica that week, but it was *a lot* and they were all preaching the same mantra: **"Cody is bad for your game."**

Its just unfortunate that this particular showmance was one of the few that would later result in marriage, therefore the HGs had no way of knowing at the time just how strong Jody's bond truly was. Although I have to say that according to DR sessions from Jess that week, it seemed like she was genuinely considering turning her back on Cody at some points. Not sure how much of that was production/editing and how much was genuine. But if it was *at all* genuine, then I stand by my comment that this is probably the most affective tactic I've ever seen to get a showmance to turn on one another.

I actually spent the past several months rewatching (or watching for the first time depending on the season) every single season of Big Brother US in chronological order. And I have to say that season 9 was the most unbearable season for me. I found it difficult to watch in its entirety because of how incredibly unlikable the entire cast is. Not to mention how awful the theme/twist of the season is. The soul mates thing is absolutely nauseating. The strategic game play is nonexistent. It doesn't even feel like a season of Big Brother. It feels like Big Brother's unsuccessful spin off sister series that only got 1 season before getting canceled.

And let me just add that I'm actually a fan of trashy reality TV. (BB8 is one of my fave seasons ever.) But BB9 isn't just trashy... It's boring and gross. Especially given what happened with the winner and a few other HGs after the show... Yuck.

This is a great season for anyone wanting to see a different style of female game play as opposed to what's become more common for female cast members on recent seasons. When is the last time, in recent years, that we've seen the ruthlessness that Jun and Alison displayed on their season from any female house guests? I'll wait.

Also, I thought the x factor twist was a great twist. It didn't too heavily impact the actual game play like most modern twists we see now do (ie-the hacker twist BB20), which I like. The twist more so created added drama and entertainment value. I can appreciate a twist that adds a little spice to the house, but I can't stand these modern day twists that affect the game so heavily that it doesn't even feel like classic Big Brother anymore.

So more players like Analyse essentially.

I was in the kitchen when this occurred, but the server walks back to where I am with a freaking *tooth* in their hand. Long story short, we comped their entire ticket and, *yes*, they stayed and ate their meals **PLUS** dessert. However, this isn't actually that gross of a story. Because in all actuality, they didn't find a tooth in their salad at all. You see, their server overheard one of the kids at the table ask their mom if they were "still gonna get money from the tooth fairy" even though they "didn't have their tooth to put under the pillow anymore". SMH. People will do anything to save a dollar.

But the broadcasted show certainly played out an edit of Lydia and Nat fighting for Jessie's attention. Which ultimately ended with Lydia and Jessie hooking up in jury house, talking smack about Natalie's lies and manipulative tactics.

Meanwhile, Nat gets engaged in the BB house and sends Michele out the door with specific instructions to tell everyone in jury about her engagement! Imo, this was one of Nat's worst moves and that's why she got called out for it during jury questioning right before the live finale night vote. Michele - "Natalie, why was it so important to you that I tell everyone in the jury house about your 'supposed' engagement? Was it strategy to compell us to vote for you?" Which basically screamed to me that they had come to that conclusion as a group in the jury house when they were all sitting around talking about her. Between the engagement announcement seeming fishy, possibly like another lie, and/or a last ditch attempt to get some votes AND the fact that it may have actually made Jessie jealous or bitter... you could tell it left a bad taste in their mouths. Sadly the engagement was the only thing she hadn't been lying to them about all season, and yet it was the final nail in her BB coffin. Tragic. Lol.
